messages:
sam_irwin: quick check — we need to pick regions for the next 6mo reserved GPU commit. looking at us-west2, eu-west1, and asia-southeast1. which tradeoffs should we care about besides sticker price?

jia_wang: latency requirements per customer? some EU customers need <60ms. APAC has smaller volume but high peak variance.

manuel_ops: also consider inter-region egress and peering. eu->us backups blew up last month — estimate ~20% extra on monthly bill when we shifted traffic.

ops-finance: short numbers I pulled: p4d on us-west2: $2.80/hr list, 35% reserved vCPU/GPU commit discount; eu-west1: $3.05/hr, 30% commit; asia-southeast1: $2.60/hr but network egress 25% higher for outbound to US. these are committed-node style pricing from vendor sheet.

sam_irwin: nice. can we run a simple cost-per-effective-token calc? we've got different utilization profiles per region.

ops-finance: minimal calc pasted: ```region | list/hr | commit% | effective/hr at 80% util
us-west2 | 2.80 | 35% | 2.80*(1-0.35)/0.8 = $2.26/hr per effective
eu-west1 | 3.05 | 30% | 3.05*(1-0.30)/0.8 = $2.67/hr
asia-southeast1 | 2.60 | 25% | 2.60*(1-0.25)/0.75 = $2.60/hr (util assumed 75%)```

neha_platform: note asia calc uses lower util assumption — we've historically seen cold starts and bursty ML load there. also GPU preemptions in some APAC zones cause extra job restarts -> effective cost up ~5-8%.

manuel_ops: networking can flip the calc. if most callers are US then hosting in APAC adds egress + latency penalties; if we place EU customers in eu-west1 we save egress and meet latency SLO.

sam_irwin: ops-bot, can you attach the last 3 months of GPU utilization per region + 95th pct latency per route?

ops-bot: uploaded: https://internal.redwood/ops/reports/gpu-util-3mo.csv and https://internal.redwood/ops/reports/latency-95th.csv :white_check_mark:

jia_wang: looked at the CSVs — us-west has steady 78% avg util, eu-west spiky with 62% avg but 90th spikes to 95%, apac 44% avg with big variance.

ops-finance: with that, committing heavy in US gives best unit economics. but we can carve smaller reservation for EU (can be smaller size but pinned) to cover spikes, and keep APAC mostly on-demand with burst credits.

sam_irwin: what about regional capacity constraints? are there GPU supply limits or quota pushes in eu-west1 for p4d?

manuel_ops: vendor told us eu-west1 has limited commit availability next quarter — they'd give 40% of requested commit until Q4. so big commit there might not materialize.

neha_platform: suggestion: commit 60% of planned capacity in us-west2 (core serving), 20% in eu-west1 dedicated for latency-sensitive EU customers, and 0-10% in apac with on-demand fallback + cheaper instance families for non-latency workloads.

ops-finance: projected monthly savings vs all-on-demand: commit plan saves ~22% overall. switching 10% more to eu increases savings by only 1.5% but introduces risk due to limited supply (and higher unit price).

sam_irwin: action items: 1) @ops-finance produce a 12-week commit vs on-demand cashflow model per-region (include egress overlay). 2) @manuel_ops check vendor commitment SLAs + provisioning timelines for eu-west1. 3) @jia_wang & @neha_platform map customer latency SLOs to candidate regions.

jia_wang: I'll start mapping SLOs and signal which routes must be eu-hosted.

manuel_ops: will ping vendor and get hard availability numbers + any early-exit clauses.

ops-finance: I'll run the cashflow model and post a short deck by EOD tomorrow.

sam_irwin: perfect. one more thought — can we model hybrid placements where we reserve cheaper, older gen GPUs in APAC for background batch and keep newest gen in US/EU? tradeoffs?

neha_platform: yes — we can tier serving: older quantized models on cheaper instances in apac for embedding jobs, keep full float gen in us/eu for real-time. need benchmark matrix but doable.

sam_irwin: cool. keep the thread updated and tag me when the deck is up. :eyes:
